evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692
evidence.field: 水 entry; PDF p. 970; printed p. 955; graphic history and meaning history
evidence.text: The scan-checked 水 entry calls the graph pictographic and says it first appears in Shang oracle-bone script. It describes varying forms, with a winding stroke for flowing water and side dots for droplets; Zhou-to-Qin forms broadly retain this picture, while Han forms move toward a straighter stroke and connected droplet marks. Separately, it proposes 河流 ‘river’ as the original meaning, then describes extension to rivers generally, water as a transparent liquid, and other liquids. It reports oracle-bone examples used for flooding or flood disaster. Thus the book’s claim about first graphic appearance is distinct from its proposed original sense; the reported flood examples are not stated to establish that sense’s priority.
evidence.title: 字源 (2012 edition; ISBN 9787552800692)

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 水 entry; 形義通解; oracle-bone and bronze uses
evidence.text: The inspected entry analyzes the graph as flowing water, with a central stroke for the flow and side dots for droplets; it notes variation in form and droplet count. It reports Shang oracle use for water disaster in 合集 10150, a ritual use in 合集 14407, and a disputed verbal use in 合集 23532, read either as leveling ground with water or washing a temple. It also reports bronze 水 used as a loan for 乞 ‘request’. The page does not establish a chronological priority among the reported oracle uses or the disputed verb’s relation to the water noun.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 水

evidence.field: 水 entry; transmitted Shuowen explanation and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The page gives the Shuowen explanation that 水 is glossed as 準 and associated with the north and cosmological imagery of multiple waters flowing together with subtle yang qi. Duan Yucai links the gloss to water’s level surface. This is evidence for the historical dictionary account, not independent confirmation of the graph’s original pictorial construction.
evidence.title: 說文解字「水」

gaps: The cited Shang examples are not individually dated in the inspected sources. Neither source establishes which semantic use is earliest; retain Shang water/flood and other reported uses as historical evidence without assigning earliest-attested priority to 河流 or flood/disaster.
